negative_reviews.author: Hajra Wahla
negative_reviews.text: Went in with family for the first time . Very poor service . They took more than 40 mins just for the dessert . Food was average .

negative_reviews.author: Harrison Mudge
negative_reviews.text:
Went for the first time today. Had the tonkatsu ramen and salmon sushi.
Sushi was nice. It had a lightly fried batter outer which gave it a nice crisp crunch and the cooked salmon centre was nice too. Sadly the wasabi on the side that it came with was more sweet than hot. Personally I like my wasabi hot.
Then the ramen as my main, all I can really say is it was exceedingly mid. The broth. Was nice, not particularly salty or strong but it was nice. The noodles didn’t really absorb much of the flavour though and the pork while flavourful was a bit tough.
To answer the question of would I have if all again, then the answer would be no sadly.
I also personally hate when they automatically add a service charge to the bill, forcing you to have to ask to have it removed.

issues: Leicester took £30.9K at 24.5% wage, and Michael flagged it as a stagnant site with covers down by over 600 from peak months, asking marketing for a full action plan built on spend, ad and influencer data (Admin Meeting 23/11).
Weekday trade from Monday to Wednesday is down most at Leicester; Google profile views rose 83%, but direction requests and venue clicks fell 50%, profile website clicks 62% and search clicks 59%.

On street and delivery flyer outreach has not worked, so Leicester moves to a full digital approach with targeted 50% Slerp and 30% delivery offers, outreach to lapsed guests, a paid influencer, Leicester BID and halal community outreach.

Leicester PMAX had the lowest CTR at 1.92% (Birmingham 5.68%, Nottingham 7.21%) and conversions fell from 1,270 to 540; a 6 mile targeting radius and a £1,000 a month UGC and influencer budget for six months were approved (Weekly DPM meeting 24/11).
A holding GM and an AGM in training are in place, with Google reviews and labour control improving (Admin Meeting 23/11).

B2B: in person outreach and a Christmas bookings email push ran, a £640 corporate booking is waiting on invoice payment, and a 15% Highcross app discount was set up (Amy's weekly report 16/11 to 22/11).

Sushi chef recruitment was boosted, new starter Mapal training was checked, Amy ran a kitchen audit on 18/11, and the site was prepared with Sophie for Teddy and Michael's audit on 20/11 (Amy's and Sophie's weekly reports).

Sales were lower ahead of Black Friday, labour reached 25.59% from unrecorded breaks and shift finish times not adjusted, and food cost rose to 23% after delayed DPD deliveries of boba and nori (England KPI meeting 24/11).

A 1 star Google review covered kitchen staffing during a post cinema rush, and on Sunday 22/11 food waits reached 30 minutes when a chef left early and two chefs were overwhelmed by a large table, to be handled with proper bill comping (England KPI meeting 24/11 and AM Updates 25/11).

Reviews improved to 90% positive with many mentioning the new GM, and a meeting with shopping centre marketing and the nearby cinema is planned to build cinema bundles for Friday and Sunday trade (AM Updates 25/11).
Disputed Deliveroo orders rose, with five refunds recovered and three pending, and Deliveroo stickers were moved from the outside walls to the sushi area to cut rider waits.
Hot water maintenance was under way, the window cleaning was poor so weekly professional cleaning is needed, and Christmas decorations are installed or arriving within days.
A part time Christmas cover candidate did well on a trial shift, and Co will be trained on sushi for the Christmas period.

Regional decisions 24/11: launch deals are suspended until a January review, sites close at 5pm on Christmas Eve with last orders at 4:30pm and double pay for the whole day, Christmas and New Year rotas must be released, and every review must be answered within 24 hours (England KPI meeting 24/11).
